tpms.when: 2009–2011 CLS (first generation) with tire pressures shown in the cluster and a reset button
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the tire and loading sticker on the driver's door pillar (or inside the fuel filler flap).
Switch the ignition on and stay parked.
Use the steering wheel buttons to page to the standard display (the one with the odometer).
Use the other pair of steering wheel arrow buttons to scroll until each tire's pressure shows. If it says the pressures appear only after driving, drive a few minutes first.
Press the reset button. The display asks whether to restart the tire pressure monitor.
Confirm with the steering wheel button the display indicates. It then shows that the tire pressure monitor has restarted.
Drive for a few minutes. The car checks the pressures and stores them as the new reference.
tpms.note: Checked in the 2009 and 2011 owner's manuals. If wheels were swapped around, a pressure may show at the wrong corner for a few minutes of driving. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.
